chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: Playing drums and filling in sections at the Savoy
summary: He took the drums and played others' books on the last hour.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Right. Now, did you find that it was easier for you to sit down at the drums and set the mood for that number, than it would be to get somebody else to do it?
Yeah. What was your reason for taking the drums?
Well, I wanted to be on the record, you know, for doing something. You know?

So, I knew at that time that I could get this right in the mood. That's what I wanted to do. So, I, cause I, back in the Savoy Ballroom, I used to, on our last hour, cause we had to play the hour before closing. I used to go out and say Harwood, you go on out and enjoy yourself." I'd sit down and

play his, his book for an hour. You know, one night, on the baritone sax. And then maybe another night, if I felt like it, I'd get back in the trombone section. That's according to how I felt. I'd say Bob, go on out and enjoy yourself. I'd go back and play the trombone book cause I wanted to keep up on those things at that time.
How did you keep up all those embouchures (inaudible)?

Well, after certain, after so many years, I figured it would be best for me to leave it alone. But, I kept it up pretty good. It was a little rough when I started back to my trumpet till I got used to it a little cause you had the sax, the trombone, the mouthpiece was much larger. And, it gave me a little trouble. But, after a certain length of time, I said well, I had enough.
(Inaudible), and I said well, I had enough.
